topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text: The boundary of my space, the familiar earth under my paws, the air thick with the scent of home—this I know. When the other comes, large and looming, asking for a part of what I guard, my fur bristles unseen. The ground shifts beneath my feet, though it hasn’t moved. The trees seem to whisper, their leaves rustling in the wind, as if they too question the stranger’s words. I hold still, watching, the heaviness in my chest unyielding. The world narrows to this moment, this space, and the silent question: how does this change the rules of this land?
